_meta.role: 2027 Graduate Software, Firmware & AI Engineering Internship

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering candidate at Rochester Institute of Technology with hands-on firmware and embedded software experience across STM32, Jetson, and Arduino platforms. Built bare-metal embedded C firmware on STM32 microcontrollers, real-time task coordination with FreeRTOS, and low-level systems programming over UART/I2C/SPI. Applied AI/ML techniques (TensorRT, quantization, YOLO) inside real-time embedded pipelines and validated system behavior through structured debugging and root-cause analysis.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition embedded system for hands-free cursor control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; debugged and resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.
Architected a Mixed Reality headset concept using AI-based real-time chroma keying; produced full technical claims documentation.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used Git-based version control (GitLab) and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system on a Jetson+Arduino embedded controller, integrating faster-whisper STT and TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2x speedup) for visual servoing.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in embedded C++ on Arduino, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection via dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over an I2C (TCA9548A) mux.
Debugged and resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) through root-cause analysis; validated 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Deployed the Jetson-side firmware bridge as a systemd service with auto-restart and non-root isolation, using static IP networking for reliable multi-device communication.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Built embedded firmware on STM32 running FreeRTOS with mutex-coordinated tasks, driving multi-servo PWM control from interrupt-driven UART commands sent by a Jetson running YOLOv8 object detection.
Integrated VL53L0X time-of-flight sensing and OLED distance visualization into the real-time embedded control loop.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built low-level systems firmware in bare-metal embedded C on an STM32 Cortex-M4 microcontroller, programming GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, and I2C1 peripherals directly at the register level.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and an interrupt-driven I2C sampling pipeline; validated deterministic 1 Hz operation in Proteus at 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM.

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Applied 8-bit quantization (bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) to a 1.1B-parameter language model, reducing GPU memory footprint by ~55% with under 1% accuracy degradation.
